mainEntity.name: What does a crypto presale marketing agency actually do?

acceptedAnswer.text: A presale marketing agency builds the demand and credibility stack a project needs before a public token sale opens. That means: a media narrative placed in tier-1 outlets to establish legitimacy, KOL coordination across Twitter/X, YouTube and Telegram to reach retail buyers, and community mechanics to hold interest through the launchpad window. Shilika Jain runs this as a fractional senior operator directly for $5K–$12K/month, or as a defined sprint at $15K–$40K.

mainEntity.name: How much does crypto presale marketing cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A fractional senior operator running your full presale comms costs $5K–$12K per month. A defined launch sprint covering six to eight weeks around the presale window costs $15K–$40K. KOL spend sits on top of that: nano-tier posts run $200–$1.5K each, micro-tier $500–$5K, mid-tier $10K–$30K and macro-tier $25K–$100K-plus. The right mix depends on your launchpad target audience and the size of the presale raise.

mainEntity.name: Which outlets and channels can you get my presale into?

acceptedAnswer.text: For editorial: CoinDesk, Cointelegraph, The Block, Decrypt, Blockworks and The Defiant for tier-1 crypto; Forbes, Benzinga and Yahoo Finance where a mainstream angle exists. For APAC: BloomingBit and TokenPost (Korea), CryptoTimes JP and CoinPost (Japan), ChainCatcher and Jinse (China), Inc42 (India), e27 (SEA). For KOLs: a vetted roster of 200-plus across Twitter/X, YouTube and Telegram spanning nano to macro tiers.

mainEntity.name: When should I start presale PR?

acceptedAnswer.text: Six to twelve weeks before the presale opens is the minimum workable window. That is when positioning can be set, journalist relationships can be built and embargo lead time can be secured. Starting two weeks out means you are relying entirely on KOLs with no editorial credibility layer, which reduces conversion from informed buyers and can complicate launchpad due diligence.
